stances.claim: Both SC unconstitutionality declaration AND congressional repeal are needed -- not either-or -- because the Constitution bars irrepealable laws, meaning future Congresses could revive pork barrel after Drilon/Belmonte's terms end; only SC unconstitutionality provides a more durable (though not absolute) bar.
stances.rhetorical_move: both-and-not-either-or framing (escaping the binary the question posed)

stances.claim: Justices are better guardians than lawmakers against pork revival because of 'cold neutrality' and 'no pecuniary interest' in the pork barrel -- the structural-incentives argument, not a personal-virtue claim.
stances.rhetorical_move: structural-incentive comparison (institutional design over individual character)

stances.claim: The Senate resolution urging Aquino to realign unspent 2013 PDAF to augment calamity funds is constitutional under Art VI Sec 25(5) and the Administrative Code -- makes legal, political, and humanitarian sense.

BUT if the SC declares PDAF unconstitutional, the unspent funds cease to be 'appropriated funds' and revert to unappropriated general funds -- which cannot be realigned because realignment presupposes appropriation; thus the Senate's realignment plan would be legally orphaned.
stances.rhetorical_move: contingent-legal-trap identification (showing how a desired outcome becomes self-defeating under a probable future ruling)

stances.claim: The safer course is for Congress to pass a supplemental budget or new law authorizing line agencies to use the savings -- only Congress can appropriate, neither the President nor the SC can spend unappropriated funds without enabling legislation.
stances.rhetorical_move: safer-path recommendation (offering forward-compatible remedy under multiple SC-ruling scenarios)

stances.claim: Misspent PDAF prior to the TRO can still be recovered -- COA or the judiciary in appropriate proceedings can order refunds as 'fruits of a void or nonexistent law,' should the SC declare PDAF unconstitutional.
stances.rhetorical_move: recovery-mechanism mapping (closing the loop from unconstitutionality to fund recovery)

notable_anecdotes: The 'cold neutrality... no pecuniary interest' distinction between justices and lawmakers -- the structural-incentives argument stated as Justice-vs-Legislator institutional comparison, not a virtue claim. The phrasing positions the SC as more reliable not because justices are better people but because they don't personally benefit from pork.

The constitutional bar on irrepealable laws as the technical reason future Congresses can revive pork -- the moment where a procedural-constitutional rule becomes the strategic argument for SC over Congress as the more durable abolisher.

The contingent-trap framing of the Senate realignment proposal: it works only if PDAF survives constitutional challenge, and is legally orphaned if PDAF doesn't. The savings become 'fruits of a void or nonexistent law' -- a phrase whose legal-organic vocabulary makes void-ness feel almost decomposable.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban rejects the false binary of SC-or-Congress and argues both must act on pork barrel. If Congress alone repeals (as Senate President Franklin Drilon and Speaker Feliciano Belmonte have committed), the Constitution's bar on irrepealable laws means future Congresses could revive pork once Drilon and Belmonte's terms end. Only an SC unconstitutionality declaration provides a more durable bar, because justices have 'cold neutrality' and 'no pecuniary interest' in pork -- a structural-incentives argument, not a virtue claim. Turning to the unspent 2013 PDAF (senators waived allocations; SC TRO blocked releases), he validates the Senate resolution urging President Aquino to realign these savings to augment existing calamity funds under Constitution Art VI Sec 25(5) and the Administrative Code of 1987 -- the move makes legal, political, and humanitarian sense for Bohol/Cebu earthquake survivors. BUT he identifies a contingent legal trap: if the SC declares PDAF unconstitutional, the unspent funds cease to be 'appropriated funds' and revert to unappropriated general funds, which cannot be realigned because realignment presupposes appropriation. The 'safer solution' is for Congress to pass a supplemental budget or new law authorizing line agencies to use the savings -- only Congress can appropriate; neither the President nor the SC can spend unappropriated funds. As to PDAF allegedly misspent prior to the TRO, COA or the judiciary may order refunds as 'fruits of a void or nonexistent law.'
